My Days Of
Stark Terror!

Russian Victim Of
Brutal Treatment
Describes Cruelty

By OSCAR FAINBERG
As Told To
GEORGE LEONOF

(Oscar Fainberg, 27, a piece goods salesman, is well-known to the writer of this remarkable, revealing article of medieval bestiality by Russian emigre elements under Japanese rule in Tientsin. It is a repetition of the rule of terror in Harbin following the Japanese annexation of Manchuria. The truth of the story has been borne out by medical practitioners, who testify to the beating suffered by Fainberg—Ed.)

I HAD heard of the "Russkiy Dom," and the ruthless treatment of Russian emigres by their own people in North China even before I thought of embarking for Tientsin to visit my parents. Yet, when I sailed on May 2 by the Jardine, Matheson ship Tai Sang, I would never have imagined, even in moments of wildest fantasy, with what sadistic cruelty and inhuman viciousness I and others in my plight were to be treated.

On board the Tai Sang the captain told me that I would encounter trouble because of my passport, which was issued in Tientsin in 1937 by the Chinese Government; I was worried, but it was too late then to take any action.

The Tai Sang arrived at Tangku at 5 p.m. on May 5. We could not enter because of the low tide, and passengers were informed that they would have to wait till the next morning. As an alternative, however, they could land and entrain on the Fusan Express, which would take them to Tientsin in 30 or 40 minutes. All the passengers, and among them I, decided on this latter course.

When the Fusan Express steamed away from the Tangku station two hours later, a Russian gendarme, member of the Japanese-commanded Special Branch Railway Police but dressed in mufti, began to inspect the passports of all passengers on the train, nationality regardless.

Coming to me, he took my passport issued by the Kuomintang in Tientsin. Glancing through it he said nothing, then told me that he would return it in five minutes and left.

（奥斯卡·法因伯格，27岁，布匹推销员，本文作者对这篇揭露天津日占统治下俄国流亡分子中世纪般兽行的非凡文章中的主人公十分熟悉。这是继日本吞并满洲后哈尔滨恐怖统治的重演。医务工作者证实了法因伯格所遭受的殴打，从而印证了故事的真实性——编者注。）

在我动身前往天津探望父母之前，我就听说过“俄罗斯之家” (Russkiy Dom)，以及华北地区俄国流亡者对其同胞的无情虐待。然而，当我于5月2日乘坐怡和洋行 (Jardine, Matheson) 的“泰生”轮 (Tai Sang) 启航时，即便在最疯狂的幻想中，我也从未想象到我和其他处境相同的人将遭受如此施虐狂般的残忍和非人的恶毒对待。

在“泰生”轮上，船长告诉我，由于我的护照是由中国政府于1937年在天津签发的，我会遇到麻烦；我很担心，但那时采取行动为时已晚。

“泰生”轮于5月5日下午5点抵达塘沽。由于退潮，我们无法入境，乘客被告知必须等到第二天早上。不过，作为替代方案，他们可以上岸并搭乘开往釜山的特快列车，该列车将在30或40分钟内将他们送往天津。所有乘客，包括我在内，都选择了后一种方案。

两小时后，当釜山特快列车驶离塘沽站时，一名俄国宪兵——他是受日本人指挥的特别处铁路警察的成员，但身着便服——开始检查车上所有乘客的护照，不分国籍。

他走到我面前，拿走了我在天津由国民党政府签发的护照。他扫视了一遍，什么也没说，然后告诉我他五分钟后归还，随即离开。

I WAS TO PRAY
TO GOD

In approximately five minutes he returned with a uniformed Japanese soldier of the Japanese Military Police. He asked me to accompany them, with my luggage, to the gendarmerie compartment. I paled, remembering what the Tai Sang captain had told me. I still recall now the growing conviction that I would be shot, and more plainly how, later, I was to pray that God should mercifully put me out of my pain-racked misery.

In the private compartment, they systematically went through my luggage. The heels were torn from my shoes, Coat and trousers linings were ripped off. I was ordered to remove every shred of clothing.

The Russian, who, I later learned, was Nikonoff, head of the Tangku Special Branch Railway Police, was conversing with the Japanese. I could hear but little, and what I did hear lifted my rapidly-beating heart into my mouth. "He's a Russian spy," I heard Nikonoff remark casually, as though this accusation, which sounded, to me, like a death sentence, was to be taken for granted.

I was told that I would have to go to the Chinese City station in Tientsin. When we arrived, I was informed that we would not get off, but would go on to Peiping.

Throughout the trip to Tientsin I stood on my feet. Once, when I leaned against a wall, Nikonoff calmly took a riding whip which the Japanese held in his hand, struck me with stinging blows over neck and chest. "Dirty Jew," he growled, "get down on your knees."

LASHED SAVAGELY
AT MY BACK

Tears of rage and indignation swelling in my eyes, I obeyed the command. The Japanese was not to be outdone. As I kneeled, he removed his belt and lashed savagely at my back. Nikonoff stood by, drinking beer. When the Japanese satisfied himself that he had beaten me sufficiently, Nikonoff threw the remnants of his glass into my face, snarling "You'll rot, you dirty Jew."

I remained kneeling, not knowing what next to expect, for three hours before we arrived at Peiping. As the train came to a standstill, my hands were tied behind my back, and we got off. I was pushed into a car with six armed Japanese and Nikonoff. We traveled for an hour before we arrived at a building which, I later learned, was the Chinese police barracks.

Here I was told to sit with Chinese policemen, and not dare to move. I remained there, naked, cold and hungry, until the next day, May 6, 7 a.m. At this hour I received a visit from "Commander" Ivanoff, whom I had heard about. He is known as a "Sadist".

Throwing down some paper and a pen, he ordered me harshly to write my biography, telling me he would return in an hour to collect it. Hurriedly I wrote of everything, from the day of my birth, that I could remember of my life. In an hour Ivanoff came for the papers and left. He returned in five minutes with a heavy stick, commanding me to accompany him.

我曾向上帝
祈祷

大约五分钟后，他和一名身穿制服的日本宪兵一起回来了。他要求我带着行李随他们去宪兵车厢。我脸色苍白，想起了“泰生”轮船长的话。我至今仍记得那种越来越强烈的确信：我将被枪决；更清晰的是，后来我是如何祈祷上帝仁慈地结束我这充满痛苦的悲惨境遇。

在私人包厢里，他们系统地搜查了我的行李。鞋跟被从鞋子上撕下，大衣和裤子的衬里被扯掉。我被命令脱掉每一片衣物。

那个俄国人，我后来得知他是塘沽特别处铁路警察负责人尼科诺夫 (Nikonoff)，正在与日本人交谈。我只能听到只言片语，而听到的内容让我狂跳的心提到了嗓子眼。“他是个俄国间谍，”我听到尼科诺夫漫不经心地说道，仿佛这一对我而言如同死刑判决般的指控是理所当然的。

我被告知必须去天津的中国城车站。当我们到达时，我得知我们不下车，而是继续前往北平。

在前往天津的整个旅途中，我一直站着。有一次，当我靠在墙上时，尼科诺夫 calmly 拿过日本人手中的马鞭，狠狠地抽打我的脖子和胸部。“肮脏的犹太人，”他咆哮道，“跪下。”

背部遭到
野蛮鞭打

愤怒和屈辱的泪水在眼中涌动，我服从了命令。那个日本人也不甘示弱。当我跪下时，他解下皮带，野蛮地抽打我的背部。尼科诺夫站在一旁喝着啤酒。当日本人认为自己打得足够多时，尼科诺夫将杯中残酒泼到我脸上，狞笑着说：“你会烂掉的，你这肮脏的犹太人。”

在抵达北平之前，我跪了三个小时，不知道接下来会发生什么。当火车停稳时，我的双手被反绑在背后，我们下了车。我被推进一辆汽车，车里有六名武装日本人和尼科诺夫。我们行驶了一个小时，才到达一栋建筑，我后来得知那是中国警察营房。

在这里，我被要求和中國警察坐在一起，不敢动弹。我就那样赤身裸体、又冷又饿地待在那里，直到第二天，5月6日早上7点。在这个时间，我迎来了听说过的“指挥官”伊万诺夫 (Ivanoff) 的探访。他以“施虐狂”闻名。

他扔下一些纸和一支笔，严厉命令我写下我的生平，告诉我他一小时后来取。我匆忙写下了从我出生那天起所能记得的一切生活经历。一小时后，伊万诺夫来取走文件并离开了。五分钟后，他带着一根粗棍子回来，命令我随他走。

TAKEN INTO BLEAK
DAMP CELLAR

We went into the compound and en-
tered another building. Here we de-
scended into a deep cellar through many
bleak, damp rooms and corridors. Finally
we arrived at a small iron door. As we
entered I saw that there were no win-
dows. A smoking kerosene lamp contri-
buted an ominous, flickering light. An
iron bar had been built into two op-
posite walls across the room, just under
the ceiling. There were iron handlocks
on one wall, just above a bath which
was built into the floor.

The only furniture in the room was
an iron table and a wooden deck chair
which I later learned to dread, while in
a corner lay small sacks containing, I
later discovered, peas, unrefined salt and
rice. On the iron table stood an inkwell.
Other implements included pens and pen-
cils, pocket-knives, three rubber batons,
thin bamboo rods and hacksaw blades.

“Sadist” Ivanoff commanded me to
strip completely naked. I did so. His
next act was to tie my hands behind my
backs at the biceps, he then took a long
rope, tied one end to the cord which
bound me, and threw the free end over
the iron bar under the ceiling. Ivanoff
then kicked me viciously from the back.
As I stumbled forward, he hoisted me up.
I dangled in the air, my feet five inches
from the floor. As the weight of my
body dragged me lower and lower, my
biceps began to stretch abnormally. I
was in agony.

But I soon forgot this pain. It was
driven from my body by an agony far
more intense when Ivanoff pushed me
and commenced beating my kidneys with
the long, heavy stick he had been carry-
ing as I swung to and fro.

ARMS WERE BLUE
AND BLOODLESS

I caught a glimpse of his face as
he beat me. The “sadist” had a clean-
shaven head. His eyes, blood-red, were
savagely protruding. Saliva trickled from
his mouth. Just then the long stick
broke, and he began beating me, still
aiming for the kidneys, with a rubber
baton. My arms were blue, bloodless. At
the right wrist a vein had become swollen
to nearly the size of an apple. After
what seemed like hours, but was actually
15 minutes of consistent beating, I lost
consciousness. Throughout the savage
beating Ivanoff had not asked me a single
question.

I came to on the cement floor of the
torture chamber with a racking pain in
my head. I put my hand to it and felt
a huge bump. Evidently I was let down
suddenly and far from gently. Blood
was trickling from my nose; agonizing
shooting pains in the chest and kidneys
almost forced me into merciful oblivion
again, but I was not fortunate enough to
lose consciousness. I attempted to rise,
but collapsed. I suddenly noticed that
the nails on my toes were black. Closer
inspection revealed that they had been
burned. Apparently this had been the
“Sadist’s” method of bringing me to.
Suddenly I felt that my toes pained me.
I had not noticed the pain previously for
the greater agony in my suffering chest
and kidneys.

被带入阴冷
潮湿的地窖

我们走进大院，进入另一栋建筑。在这里，我们穿过许多阴冷潮湿的房间和走廊，下到深深的地窖。最后，我们来到一扇小铁门前。进去后，我看到没有窗户。一盏冒烟的煤油灯发出不祥的闪烁光芒。一根铁杆横跨房间建在两面相对的墙上，就在天花板下方。一面墙上装有铁手铐，就在嵌入地板的浴缸上方。

房间里唯一的家具是一张铁桌和一把木制躺椅，我后来对它充满了恐惧，而在角落里放着几个小袋子，我后来发现里面装着豌豆、粗盐和米。铁桌上放着一个墨水瓶。其他工具包括钢笔和铅笔、小折刀、三根橡胶警棍、细竹竿和钢锯条。

“施虐狂”伊万诺夫命令我完全脱光衣服。我照做了。他的下一个动作是将我的双手在二头肌处反绑在背后，然后拿起一根长绳，将一端系在绑我的绳子上，将自由端抛过天花板下的铁杆。伊万诺夫随后从背后狠狠踢了我一脚。当我向前踉跄时，他将我吊起。我悬在空中，双脚离地五英寸。随着我身体的重量将我越拉越低，我的二头肌开始异常拉伸。我痛苦不堪。

但我很快忘记了这种疼痛。当伊万诺夫推搡我，并在我来回摆动时用他一直拿着的那根又长又重的棍子殴打我的肾脏时，更剧烈的痛苦驱散了之前的痛感。

双臂变得青紫
毫无血色

在他殴打我时，我瞥见了他的脸。这个“施虐狂”剃光了头。他的双眼血红，凶狠地凸出。口水从他的嘴角流下。就在这时，长棍断了，他开始用橡胶警棍继续殴打我，目标仍然是肾脏。我的双臂变得青紫，毫无血色。右手腕上的一根静脉肿胀得几乎有苹果那么大。经过看似数小时、实则持续15分钟的连续殴打后，我失去了知觉。在整个野蛮的殴打过程中，伊万诺夫没有问过我一个问题。

我在刑讯室的水泥地板上醒来，头部剧痛。我用手摸了摸，感觉有一个巨大的肿块。显然，我是被突然且毫不轻柔地放下来的。血从鼻子里流出；胸部和肾脏传来的剧烈刺痛几乎迫使我再次陷入仁慈的昏迷，但我没有那么幸运失去知觉。我试图站起来，但瘫倒了。我突然注意到脚趾甲是黑色的。仔细检查后发现它们曾被烧灼。显然，这是“施虐狂”让我苏醒的方法。突然，我感到脚趾疼痛。此前由于胸部和肾脏遭受的巨大痛苦，我没有注意到这种疼痛。

AGAIN BEATEN
BY ANOTHER MAN

I lay on the floor for five minutes
before I heard steps and voices outside
the door. "Now he'll talk," a voice said.

The door opened, and I saw a huge,
hairy figure of a man. I knew him also—
it was Pavil Chernisheff, who formerly
had been a provider of women for foreign
sailors in Tientsin, a notorious loafer and
trouble-maker. He was a man of unusual
physical strength, with one eye—the other
is of glass—crooked feet and a shaven
head.

Leaning over me, he struck me on
the face with his fist, shouting, "Take
that, you dirty Jew, for Russian blood
spilled in Russia."

With him was Boris Ignatenko, whom
I knew in Harbin as a reporter of Our
Road, a Russian fascist paper. Igna-
tenko stood aside.

Chernisheff started the same pro-
cedure. He tied my arms, by the biceps,
behind my back—the cord cutting into
raw flesh—and once again lifted me off
the floor. Taking the thin bamboo sticks
from the table, he commenced beating
my toes.

TELL US WHO
YOU WORK FOR!

Ignatenko sat down at the table and
addressed me, "Tell us whom you are
working with." At the time I did not
realize the full significance of the ques-
tion, and replied that I was a salesman
for a foreign firm.

"Give us names," Ignatenko ordered,
and I mentioned Whiteaway, Laidlaw,
Hall and Holtz, Aren Fein, Zaslavsky,
Wing On, Lun Chong and others. Cher-
nisheff commenced beating me more
savagely. "We want names, understand?"
he shouted.

The beating was suddenly interrup-
ted by the entry into the dungeon of
Leonid Nikolaevich Guttman, whose
parents, Jews, were converted by the
Russian Orthodox Church, I was told. He
is the head of the Special Branch Rail-
way Police, and the God and Tsar of
Russian emigres in North China. Gutt-
man also carried a stick. As he entered,
he struck me a heavy blow across the
chest with the greeting, "Hello, Jew," and
sat down.

Meanwhile, Chernisheff continued the
beating as Guttman drew from his pocket
the visiting cards confiscated from me.
The first card was that of Mr. Hal P.
Mills. Questioned, I told them that he
was an American, a theatrical agent.
"You lie—you bastard," shouted Cherni-
sheff as he intensified the beating.

MILLS ACCUSED
AS CHINESE SPY

Guttman and Ignatenko sprung from
their seats at the table and approached
me. "You lie, he's a Chinese spy," Gutt-
man accused. "Tell us why he sent you
to North China. Mind you, we know
all—you'd better not lie or you'll rot to
death!"

I told them that my relations with
him were purely of a business nature, and
that I had inserted advertisements in
his paper. I had not meant to mention
that Mr. Mills is a publisher of a paper,
but I slipped up. Fortunately they pass-
ed it by, but insisted, "You lie! how much
does he pay you? What is his attitude
toward the Japanese?" I could give no
answer, and was beaten the more for it.
pages.zh:
再次遭到
另一名男子殴打

我在地板上躺了五分钟，才听到门外有脚步声和说话声。“现在他会招供了，”一个声音说道。

门开了，我看到了一个高大、多毛的男人身影。我也认识他——他是帕维尔·切尔尼谢夫 (Pavil Chernisheff)，以前曾在天津为外国水手提供妇女，是个臭名昭著的懒汉和惹事生非者。他体力过人，一只眼睛是假的（另一只是玻璃眼），双脚畸形，剃着光头。

他俯身向我，用拳头猛击我的脸部，喊道：“挨这一下，你这肮脏的犹太人，为了在俄国流洒的俄国人的血。”

和他在一起的是鲍里斯·伊格纳坚科 (Boris Ignatenko)，我在哈尔滨时就认识他，他是俄国法西斯报纸《我们的道路》 (Our Road) 的记者。伊格纳坚科站在一旁。

切尔尼谢夫开始了同样的程序。他将我的手臂在二头肌处反绑在背后——绳子勒进皮肉里——再次将我吊离地面。他从桌上拿起细竹竿，开始抽打我的脚趾。

告诉我们你
为谁工作！

伊格纳坚科坐在桌旁，对我说道：“告诉我们你和谁一起工作。”当时我没有完全意识到这个问题的重要性，回答说我是为一家外国公司做推销员。

“给我们名字，”伊格纳坚科命令道，我提到了白威 (Whiteaway)、莱德劳 (Laidlaw)、霍尔 (Hall) 和霍尔茨 (Holtz)、阿伦·费恩 (Aren Fein)、扎斯拉夫斯基 (Zaslavsky)、永安 (Wing On)、伦昌 (Lun Chong) 等人。切尔尼谢夫开始更野蛮地殴打我。“我们要名字，明白吗？”他喊道。

殴打突然被列昂尼德·尼古拉耶维奇·古特曼 (Leonid Nikolaevich Guttman) 进入地牢所打断，据说他的父母是犹太人，后被俄罗斯东正教会改宗。他是特别处铁路警察的负责人，也是华北俄国流亡者的上帝和沙皇。古特曼也拿着一根棍子。进来时，他用一句“你好，犹太人”的问候语重重地击打我的胸部，然后坐下。

与此同时，当古特曼从口袋里掏出从我这里没收的名片时，切尔尼谢夫继续殴打。第一张名片是哈尔·P·米尔斯 (Hal P. Mills) 先生的。受到质问时，我告诉他们他是美国人，一名戏剧代理人。“你撒谎——你这杂种，”切尔尼谢夫一边加剧殴打一边喊道。

米尔斯被指控
为中国间谍

古特曼和伊格纳坚科从桌旁跳起来，向我逼近。“你撒谎，他是中国间谍，”古特曼指控道。“告诉我们他为什么派你去华北。注意，我们知道一切——你最好别撒谎，否则你会烂死！”

我告诉他们，我与他的关系纯粹是商业性质的，我在他的报纸上刊登过广告。我本无意提及米尔斯先生是一家报纸的出版商，但我说漏了嘴。幸运的是他们忽略了这一点，但坚持说：“你撒谎！他付给你多少钱？他对日本人的态度如何？”我无法回答，因此遭到了更严厉的殴打。

The next card was that of Alexander
Engel, formerly of the Cinema Art Cor-
poration and now photographer at Far-
ren's night club. "And what is this
Comintern agent doing in Shanghai
now?" Guttman asked me. I replied
that he was taking photographs. "You
lie again," Guttman stated conclusively,
"you both spied on Japanese forces dur-
ing the conflict at Shanghai."

My next dish was the visiting card
of A. Zaslavsky, who owns a piece goods
store at 859 Avenue Joffre. "What busi-
ness did you have with this dirty Jew?"
Guttman wanted to know, "What is his
nationality?" I replied that I had sold
him piece goods, that he was an emi-
grant.

"You lying son of a bitch!" Guttman
shouted at me, "He's a Soviet citizen, his
brother is the G.P.U. head in Kharkov.
He's a G.P.U. agent! How much did he
pay you for each communication?"

FASTENED BY
LOCKS TO WALL

Resignedly, by this time, I insisted
that I only sold him piece goods, and
was let down. They untied the ropes, and
fastened me to the handlocks on the wall,
my back to the room.

"Why did you come to Tientsin?
Where is the rest of your luggage and
documents?" Ignatenko inquired. With-
out waiting for a reply, he added, "Tell
us how you communicate with the Soviet
Consulate in Tientsin? We know all,
mind you."

Mercifully, I fainted again. When I
came to once again on the floor of the
dungeon, I was untied. Leaning over me
I saw the face of "Sadist" Ivanoff.

Hoisting me to my feet, he half-drag-
ged me through a labyrinth of dark,
stinking rooms and corridors. We came
to more stairs, and descended into a
lower cellar.

Here we entered into a large, electri-
cally lighted hall, in which stood six
cages, some five feet square and four feet
wide. The entrance into these cages was
a kennel-like door, and I had to crawl
on my hands and knees to get in. As I
crawled, Ivanoff struck me with his
stick, "Why so slow, you goat of Jerusa-
lem?" he jeered.

Locking the iron cage, he shut off the
light and left.

I remained in the cage, without food
or water, for three days. Why I noticed
this I do not know, for my tortured body
would have rebelled at food, although I
occasionally wanted water.

FERVENTLY PRAYED
FOR DEATH

On May 9 Chernisheff finally put in
an appearance, ordered me out of my
cage, and led me back to the room which,
three days ago, was the altar at which
I fervently prayed for death. Here he
hurled senseless questions at me: "Whom
did you work with in Harbin? With
whom did you blow up the Sungari River
Bridge? What is your real name?"

Before I could answer the door open-
ed and two other Russians entered. I
later learned their names as Osipov and
Fadeyeff. The latter, I found out, had
been employed by the China General
Omnibus Company here as a conductor
in 1932.

Without ceremony, they ordered me
to reply to all questions put, "or we'll pour
kerosene into you," they threatened. Here
I was to discover the significance of the
wooden deck chair, so incongruous in its
sinister, damp surroundings.
pages.zh:
下一张名片属于亚历山大·恩格尔（Alexander Engel），他此前供职于电影艺术公司（Cinema Art Corporation），现在是法伦夜总会（Farren's night club）的摄影师。“这个共产国际特工现在在上海做什么？”古特曼（Guttman）问我。我回答说他在拍照。“你又在撒谎，”古特曼断然说道，“你们俩在上海冲突期间监视了日军。”

我接下来的“菜”是A. 扎斯拉夫斯基（A. Zaslavsky）的名片，他在霞飞路859号拥有一家布料店。“你和这个肮脏的犹太人有什么生意往来？”古特曼质问道，“他是哪国人？”我回答说我把布料卖给了他，他是个移民。

“你这个撒谎的狗娘养的！”古特曼对我吼道，“他是苏联公民，他的兄弟是哈尔科夫的国家政治保卫局（G.P.U.）局长。他是国家政治保卫局的特工！他每次向你购买情报付了你多少钱？”

用锁固定在墙上

此时，我已无奈地坚持说我只是卖给他布料，随后被放了下来。他们解开了绳索，将我背对着房间，铐在墙上的手铐上。

“你为什么来天津？你其余的行李和文件在哪里？”伊格纳坚科（Ignatenko）询问道。没等我回答，他又补充说：“告诉我们你是如何与苏联驻天津领事馆联络的？你要知道，我们什么都清楚。”

仁慈的是，我又昏了过去。当我再次在地牢的地板上醒来时，我被松了绑。俯视着我的是“施虐狂”伊万诺夫（Ivanoff）的脸。

他把我拽起来，半拖着我穿过迷宫般黑暗、恶臭的房间和走廊。我们来到更多的楼梯前，下到了更底层的地下室。

在这里，我们进入了一个宽敞的大厅，里面亮着电灯，立着六个笼子，每个大约五英尺见方，四英尺宽。这些笼子的入口像狗窝的门一样，我必须手脚并用地爬进去。当我爬行时，伊万诺夫用手杖打我，“怎么这么慢，你这耶路撒冷的山羊？”他讥笑道。

他锁上铁笼，关了灯，离开了。

我在笼子里待了三天，没有食物也没有水。我不明白自己为何会注意到这一点，因为我受尽折磨的身体会对食物产生排斥，尽管我偶尔想要喝水。

虔诚地祈求死亡

5月9日，切尔尼舍夫（Chernisheff）终于露面，命令我走出笼子，把我带回了那个房间——就在三天前，我还在那里虔诚地祈求死亡。在这里，他向我抛出一连串毫无意义的问题：“你在哈尔滨和谁一起工作？你和谁炸毁了松花江大桥？你的真名是什么？”

还没来得及回答，门开了，另外两名俄罗斯人走了进来。我后来得知他们的名字是奥西波夫（Osipov）和法杰耶夫（Fadeyeff）。我发现后者曾于1932年在此受雇于中国公共汽车公司（China General Omnibus Company）担任售票员。

他们毫不客气地命令我回答所有提出的问题，“否则我们就把煤油灌进你身体里，”他们威胁道。在这里，我才发现那把木制躺椅的意义所在，它与周围阴森潮湿的环境显得如此格格不入。

pages.en:
I was ordered to sit on the chair.
"How old are you?" they inquired.
"Twenty-seven," I replied. Chernisheff
was indignant: "You're 32, you lying
bastard," he insisted.
"What is your real name?" he in-
quired further.
"Oscar Fainberg."
This also he contradicted. "Lying
again," he snarled. "Your name's Grisha
'Dynamite'. Where's Popuass and Kuli-
biakin? What did you do in Harbin in
1929?"

TORTURE IS
AGAIN STARTED

I could not imagine what to reply as
to the whereabouts of the two people,
utterly unknown to me, which he named.
As to the second question, I told him I
worked with Shriro Brothers, an Ameri-
can firm in Harbin, in 1929.

But Chernisheff was in his best con-
tradictory mood. "No!" he shrieked,
"You worked for the Chinese Eastern
Railway. Tell us!"

As convincingly as I could, and fight-
ing off a feeling of oncoming hysteria, I
explained that I knew nothing of what
he spoke, that I was well known in Har-
bin since my parents had lived there for
35 years.

I may as well have said nothing. A
Chinese servant came in bearing a ket-
tle. Chernisheff took it and poured the
contents into a larger Chinese kettle
standing on a shelf in the room, which
contained kerosene, and from which I
saw extended rubber tubes. I saw him
throw in red pepper into the larger kettle,
and while panic-stricken with uncertainty
as to the effect of this new torture,
strange to me, I was puzzled.

LIQUID PUMPED
INTO NOSTRILS

I was not to be perplexed for long.
My inquisitors tied me tightly to the
chair, threw my head back and inserted
a rubber tube in each nostril.

Throbbing pains and a feeling of
nausea still come over me when I remem-
ber that drowning feeling. I felt my head
bursting—my eyes were on fire, as though
burned with red-hot pokers—my head
seemed to swell and my scalp to rise.
I began to choke and vomit as does a
drowning person, then all went black.

I regained consciousness I don't know
how much later—nor did I care. There
was a terrible pain in my ears. I found
myself breathing in short, agonizing gasps,
my nose had swollen beyond recognition
and I could not at first open my eyes.

The first people I saw when I finally
could keep my eyes open were two Rus-
sians, Kodinoff and Smirnov. Smirnov
felt my pulse and commented, "The devil
won't take him, he'll be alright."

They carried me back to my cage in
the sub-cellar. In a half hour they
brought me water and a piece of black
bread. They also tied a white cloth, on
which written Japanese characters, to my
cage.

Later that same day some Japanese
came to inspect the "zoo" with Guttman.
Among them was K. Nakamura, head of
the Special Branch Railway Police. He
conversed with Guttman in fluent Rus-
sian, then turned to the Japanese and
said, "Sovieto spy." One of the Japanese
approached my cage and spat at me.

Nakamura laughed and also approach-
ed. He held out a cigarette, but as I
reached for it Guttman struck me a hard
blow on the hand. There was general
highly amused laughter.
pages.zh:
我被命令坐在椅子上。“你多大了？”他们问道。“二十七岁，”我回答。切尔尼舍夫很愤怒：“你三十二岁了，你这个撒谎的混蛋，”他坚持道。
“你的真名是什么？”他进一步询问。
“奥斯卡·范伯格（Oscar Fainberg）。”
他也对此予以反驳。“又撒谎，”他咆哮道。“你的名字叫格里沙‘炸药’（Grisha 'Dynamite'）。波波阿斯（Popuass）和库利巴金（Kulibiakin）在哪里？你1929年在哈尔滨做了什么？”

酷刑再次开始

我无法想象该如何回答他提到的那两个我完全陌生的人的下落。关于第二个问题，我告诉他，1929年我在哈尔滨为一家美国公司什里罗兄弟公司（Shriro Brothers）工作。

但切尔尼舍夫正处于最佳的反驳状态。“不！”他尖叫道，“你在中东铁路工作。老实交代！”

我尽可能令人信服地解释，同时努力抑制即将爆发的歇斯底里感，我说我对他所说的事情一无所知，自从我的父母在那里居住了35年以来，我在哈尔滨为人所熟知。

这等于白说。一名中国仆人拿着一个水壶进来了。切尔尼舍夫接过水壶，将里面的东西倒入房间里架子上放着的一个更大的中国水壶中，那个大壶里装着煤油，我看到里面有橡胶管伸出来。我看见他把红辣椒扔进大水壶里，正当我对这种对我来说陌生的新酷刑的效果感到惊慌失措和不确定时，我感到困惑不解。

液体被泵入鼻孔

我的困惑并没有持续多久。审讯者把我紧紧绑在椅子上，把我的头向后仰，并在每个鼻孔里插入一根橡胶管。

每当回想起那种溺水的感觉，剧烈的疼痛和恶心感仍会涌上心头。我感觉头部要爆裂——双眼如火烧一般，仿佛被烧红的烙铁烫伤——头部似乎肿胀，头皮隆起。我开始像溺水者一样窒息和呕吐，然后眼前一片漆黑。

我不知道过了多久才恢复意识——我也不在乎。耳朵里剧痛难忍。我发现自己呼吸短促且痛苦，鼻子肿得面目全非，起初甚至无法睁开眼睛。

当我最终能睁开眼时，首先看到的是两个俄罗斯人，科迪诺夫（Kodinoff）和斯米尔诺夫（Smirnov）。斯米尔诺夫摸了摸我的脉搏，评论道：“魔鬼不会带走他，他会没事的。”

他们把我抬回地下室的笼子里。半小时后，他们给我送来了水和一块黑面包。他们还在我的笼子上系了一块白布，上面写着日文字符。

同一天晚些时候，一些日本人随古特曼来视察这个“动物园”。其中包括特别处铁路警察局长中村 K.（K. Nakamura）。他用流利的俄语与古特曼交谈，然后转向日本人说：“苏联间谍。”一名日本人走近我的笼子，朝我吐口水。

中村笑了，也走了过来。他递出一支香烟，但当我伸手去接时，古特曼重重地打了一下我的手。周围响起了一阵极度开心的笑声。

pages.en:
2 796

WOMEN SHRIEK
FOR HELP

I remained in the cage to May 20. Each day I was given only bread and water. At nights I used to hear hysterical shouts. "Better kill me." "I know nothing." I heard women's voices, shrieking for help, and I heard the sounds of accordions, guitars, drunken singing and laughter.

On the morning of May 20, by which time I desperately hoped that my torturers had, perhaps, forgotten of my existence, I received a visit from the "Sadist."
"What! Still alive, my dirty, little Jew? Well, get up and let's talk."

With great difficulty I crawled out, but I could not stand on my feet. I was weak and dizzy. Grasping me under my arms. Ivanoff pushed me the long way into the now familiar torture chamber. The room was full of smoke, in the center stood a fuming small stove from which protruded a red-hot poker.

At the table sat Ignatenko, pounding at a typewriter. I scarcely saw him before a blow on my jaw, delivered by someone standing at my side, threw me on the floor. I struck the cement floor head first, cutting my scalp. It was Chernisheff who had struck me.

Lifted off the floor, I was placed into the deck chair.

Again the senseless question: "Tell us with whom you worked in the chemical laboratory in Harbin and who helped you manufacture explosives," they ordered me. "Where did you get the chemicals, and whom did you deliver the explosives to?" This was accompanied by an angry threat, "Tell us everything, or you'll breathe kerosene again!"

Ignatenko was typing something. Before I could open my mouth he removed the typewritten paper and gave it to me along with others, commanding, "Read this and sign!"

ORDERED TO
SIGN CONFESSION

As I read, "Sadist" Ivanoff struck me on the face with his fist and the papers scattered on the floor. "Why don't you answer my questions?" he roared. Pausing, he struck me again. "Swine! Why did you scatter the papers?" Again I was given the papers and ordered to read.

I read myself confessing to implication in the murder of Shlubkin, a Russian policeman, in Harbin. I tried to deny it but Ignatenko shouted, "Sign!" Desperate, I threw the papers to the floor, intentionally this time.

Chernishoff and the "Sadist" seemed pleased at my obstinacy. With sudden good humor they tied me to the deck chair. Chernishoff drew a sharp pocket-knife and cut the skin above my right knee, causing a three-inch gash.
pages.zh:
2 796

妇女尖叫求救

我在笼子里一直待到5月20日。每天只给我面包和水。夜里，我经常听到歇斯底里的喊叫声。“最好杀了我。”“我什么都不知道。”我听到女人的声音，尖叫着求救，还听到手风琴、吉他、醉酒的歌声和笑声。

5月20日上午，此时我绝望地希望折磨我的人或许已经忘记了我的存在，这时“施虐狂”来访了。
“什么！还活着，我这肮脏的小犹太人？好吧，起来，我们谈谈。”

我费力地爬出来，但我站不起来。我又弱又晕。伊万诺夫抓住我的腋下，推着我走了很长一段路，进入了现在熟悉的刑讯室。房间里烟雾弥漫，中央有一个冒着烟的小炉子，从中伸出一根烧红的烙铁。

伊格纳坚科坐在桌旁，敲打着打字机。我几乎还没看清他，旁边站着的人就朝我的下巴打了一拳，把我打倒在地。我的头先撞在水泥地上，划破了头皮。打我的是切尔尼舍夫。

我被从地板上拉起来，放进躺椅里。

又是那些毫无意义的问题：“告诉我们在哈尔滨的化学实验室里你和谁一起工作，谁帮你制造炸药，”他们命令道。“你从哪里得到的化学品，你把炸药交给了谁？”伴随着愤怒的威胁，“把所有事情都交代出来，否则你又要呼吸煤油了！”

伊格纳坚科正在打字。我还没来得及开口，他就取下打印好的纸，连同其他几张一起递给我，命令道：“读这个，然后签字！”

被命令签署供词

当我阅读时，“施虐狂”伊万诺夫用拳头打我的脸，纸张散落在地板上。“你为什么不回答我的问题？”他怒吼道。停顿片刻后，他又打了我一下。“猪猡！你为什么把纸弄散？”他们再次把纸递给我，命令我阅读。

我读到我自己承认参与了在哈尔滨谋杀俄罗斯警察舒卢布金（Shlubkin）的案件。我试图否认，但伊格纳坚科喊道：“签字！”绝望之中，这次我故意把纸扔到了地板上。

切尔尼舍夫和“施虐狂”似乎对我的固执感到满意。他们突然心情大好，把我绑在躺椅上。切尔尼舍夫掏出一把锋利的折叠刀，割开我右膝上方的皮肤，造成了一道三英寸长的伤口。

pages.en:
Once again Ignatenko shouted, "Sign
those papers." But by this time I was
speechless with fright, and could move
neither tongue nor limbs. Then I began
to scream shrill and loud with panic, as
Ivanoff began to apply the red-hot poker
to the cut above my knee. Not only was
the pain so insufferable that it would not
let me sink into oblivion, but I was
mentally horrified at the bestiality of
these men. I tried to tear myself free,
but Chernishoff grasped my right hand
and Ivanoff burned the third finger.
Desperately I screamed, "I'll sign
anything!"
They released me and gave me a
glass of water to drink. "Sure, sign,"
coaxed Ignatenko, "what are you afraid
of? It's not a death warrant."
How I wished it were as I signed the
documents with a feverish, trembling
hand. I remember that I signed 15
sheets, two of which were not written on.
I was then carried back to my cage.

WOUNDS BECOME
INFECTED

Like some mangy cur, I remained in
my cage until May 29. The sore on my
knee became inflamed. There were sores
on my buttocks which would permit me
neither to lie on my back nor to sit up.
There were open sores on my sides from
the beatings.
On the night of May 29 they brought
in a new "Comintern agent." Shouting
weakly to each other when the torturers
left, we conversed. I found that he was
Sergeant Stepanoff of the Hongkong
Police, and that he was a guard on board
the British steamer Tak Sang. He had
been employed as a policeman in Hong-
kong for nine years. His ship had tied
up at Tientsin for three days, and he
went ashore to see the town. He had
British papers which certified that he
was a member of the Hongkong Police,
but he was arrested because he "had no
North China documents."
Stepanoff had gone through the same
treatment as I had. His torturers wanted to
know what the British were doing in
Hongkong, what connections they had
with the Chinese, which Britons conduct-
ed anti-Japanese agitation, and what
Russian members of the Hongkong Police
were Soviet citizens or agents.

RUSSIAN GIRL
UNDERGOES TERROR

On June 1 they brought in a 20-year-
old, pretty but miserable Russian girl. I
never learned her name, but found out
that she was arrested and cruelly beaten
because she lived with a Frenchman. The
skin on her back and legs was peeling in
thick layers. She sat in a cage comple-
tely naked.
On June 3 Stepanoff was removed
and was taken by train to the Chinese
city in Tientsin. On June 7, completely
weakened, I fainted in my cage.
That same day I was to catch my
first glimpse of paradise on earth. I was
removed to a Japanese Military Hospital in
Tientsin. The glistening white sheets,
the bed, the general cleanliness were
heavenly. It was no matter that blood
poured from my throat, that I had to
breathe steam through tubes, as long as
I could stay in hospital.
Unfortunately, they kept me there
for 13 days, and I was removed to the
Tientsin headquarters of the Special
Branch Railway Police in the Chinese
city, near the railway station.
Here I learned the names of the
Tientsin gang of inquisitors. They were
headed by Chief Inspector Roshinsky,
whose right hand man was Kaskakov.
Here were also Ignateff, Vassiliev, Mark,
Squitkin, George Chernich, brother
of my Peiping torturer, and a Japanese
muscle-man named Itoh.
pages.zh:
伊格纳坚科再次喊道：“在这些文件上签字。”但此时我吓得说不出话来，舌头和四肢都无法动弹。接着，当伊万诺夫开始将烧红的烙铁按在我膝盖上方的伤口上时，我开始因恐慌而发出尖锐大声的尖叫。不仅疼痛难以忍受，让我无法陷入昏迷，而且我对这些人的兽行感到精神上的恐惧。我试图挣脱，但切尔尼舍夫抓住了我的右手，伊万诺夫烧伤了我的第三根手指。我绝望地尖叫：“我签什么都行！”
他们放开了我，给了我一杯水喝。“当然，签吧，”伊格纳坚科哄劝道，“你怕什么？这不是死刑令。”
当我用发烧颤抖的手签署文件时，我多么希望那是死刑令啊。我记得我签了15页，其中两页是空白的。随后我被抬回笼子。

伤口感染

像一条患疥癣的杂种狗一样，我在笼子里一直待到5月29日。我膝盖上的伤口发炎了。我的臀部也有疮口，使我既不能仰卧也不能坐起。由于殴打，我的两侧也有开放性伤口。
5月29日晚，他们带来了一名新的“共产国际特工”。当折磨者离开时，我们虚弱地互相喊叫，进行交谈。我发现他是香港警队的斯蒂潘诺夫（Stepanoff）巡长，也是英国轮船“德生”号（Tak Sang）上的警卫。他在香港当了九年警察。他的船在天津停靠了三天，他上岸游览城市。他持有证明他是香港警队成员的英国证件，但他被捕是因为他“没有华北地区的证件”。
斯蒂潘诺夫经历了和我一样的待遇。他的折磨者想知道英国人在香港做什么，他们与中国人有什么联系，哪些英国人进行反日煽动，以及香港警队中哪些俄罗斯成员是苏联公民或特工。

俄罗斯女孩遭受恐怖折磨

6月1日，他们带来了一名20岁、漂亮但凄惨的俄罗斯女孩。我从未得知她的名字，但发现她因为和一个法国人同居而被捕并遭到残酷殴打。她背部和腿部的皮肤成厚层剥落。她赤身裸体地坐在笼子里。
6月3日，斯蒂潘诺夫被带走，乘火车前往天津的中国城区。6月7日，我因极度虚弱而在笼子里昏倒。
同一天，我将首次瞥见人间的天堂。我被转移到天津的一家日本陆军医院。闪亮的白床单、床铺和整体的清洁程度如同天堂一般。只要我能留在医院里，哪怕血从喉咙里涌出，哪怕我必须通过管子呼吸蒸汽，都无所谓。
不幸的是，他们只让我在那里待了13天，随后我被转移到位于火车站附近的中国城区的特别处铁路警察天津总部。
在这里，我得知了天津这群审讯者的名字。他们由督察长罗辛斯基（Roshinsky）领导，其副手是卡斯卡科夫（Kaskakov）。这里还有伊格纳捷夫（Ignateff）、瓦西里耶夫（Vassiliev）、马克（Mark）、斯奎特金（Squitkin）、乔治·切尔尼奇（George Chernich，即我在北平受审时的折磨者的兄弟），以及一名名叫伊藤（Itoh）的日本壮汉。

pages.en:
SUNBURNT TO
HIDE SCARS

The treatment here was better. I received three loaves a day and water. Here also I met Stepanoff again.
Itoh ordered us to taken out into the yard each day der that our bodies may become sunburned and thus conceal our ugly wounds to a certain extent.
In this place of confinements we had comparative peace, except that George Chernisheff made it a habit to visit us we slept and beat us with a stick.
I continued to spit blood and was attacked at short intervals with dizzy spells. Agonizing pains in my chest, kidneys and buttocks never stopped for a minute, but I had become somewhat accustomed to them.
On June 24 we were joined by another victim, 19-year-old Victor Krivoroochko. He had been brutally beaten because he possessed a Soviet registration card. In Peiping they had drowned him in the bath under the handlocks in that torture chamber which I remember so well, they drove pencils into his nostrils, burned his finger nails, but his heels and inserted horse-hairs—an agonizing experience, I was told.
Victor Krivoroochko signed everything. He promised to steal his father's Soviet passport, gave an oath that he would be their willing informer.

INFAMOUS "HOME"
NEXT VISITED

On July 3 three Russian policemen, Kozlovsky, Malandin and Verstag came for us. They put us into a car and drove to the infamous "Russkiy Dom" (Russian Home) situated on Hankow Road in the ex-German Concession of Tientsin.
We were taken down into a damp, stinking cellar where the water on the floor was ankle deep. Insects of every description crawled on the walls. We had to sit and sleep on planks placed on barrels.
Here we were given 20 cents a day each with instructions to purchase our food from Chinese puppet policemen. As the puppets extorted 15 cents only for a kettle of boiling water, we indignantly refused to eat, but spent all our money on cigarettes. Finally the Chinese took pity on us. At their own expense they occasionally brought us noodles, pieces of stale bread and matches. They even gave us a towel.
Another victim joined us on July 14. He was G. Menshik, Soviet citizen and an employee of the Peiyang Press. He was on the way to the office at 8:30 a.m. that day when Kozlovsky asked him to come to the police station for questioning. Having gone through this before, Menshik agreed. However, he was taken directly to the "Russkiy Dom." Here he was asked questions about the Soviet Consulate, his connections with the Soviet Consulate, and why he was working for the Peiyang Press, a German firm. He was also severely beaten.
He was in a terrible condition two days later, when on July 16 we were taken to the Chinese Police branch headquarters in the former German Park. Here we had two rooms and a wooden floor, for which we were thankful.
Menshik could not rise. He had been ruthlessly beaten about the kidneys and could not urinate. His stomach and eyes swelled until they seemed on the point of bursting. Half the time he was unconscious.

晒黑以掩盖伤痕

那里的待遇较好。我每天得到三个面包和水。在那里我也再次遇到了斯捷潘诺夫（Stepanoff）。
伊藤（Itoh）命令我们每天被带到院子里，以便让我们的身体被晒黑，从而在一定程度上掩盖我们难看的伤口。
在这个拘禁场所，我们享有相对的安宁，除了乔治·切尔尼谢夫（George Chernisheff）养成了一种习惯，趁我们睡觉时来访并用棍棒殴打我们。
我继续咯血，并频繁遭受眩晕发作的袭击。胸部、肾脏和臀部的剧烈疼痛从未停歇片刻，但我已对此 somewhat 习以为常。
6月24日，另一名受害者加入了我们，他是19岁的维克多·克里沃鲁奇科（Victor Krivoroochko）。他因持有一张苏联登记卡而遭到残酷殴打。在北平，他们在那间令我记忆犹新的刑讯室里，将他按在浴缸中溺水；他们将铅笔插入他的鼻孔，烧毁他的指甲和脚后跟，并插入马毛——据告知，这是一种极其痛苦的经历。
维克多·克里沃鲁奇科签署了一切文件。他承诺窃取其父亲的苏联护照，并宣誓愿意成为他们的线人。

臭名昭著的“之家”
下一站

7月3日，三名俄国警察科兹洛夫斯基（Kozlovsky）、马兰丁（Malandin）和弗尔斯塔格（Verstag）来带走我们。他们把我们塞进一辆汽车，驶往位于天津前德租界汉口路上的臭名昭著的“Russkiy Dom”（俄国人之家）。
我们被带到一个潮湿、恶臭的地窖，那里的积水深及脚踝。各种昆虫在墙壁上爬行。我们不得不坐在放在桶上的木板上，并睡在上面。
在这里，我们每人每天得到20分钱，并被指示向中国伪警察购买食物。由于伪警察仅为一壶开水就勒索15分钱，我们愤然拒绝进食，而是将所有的钱都花在香烟上。最终，这些中国人对我们产生了怜悯。他们自掏腰包，偶尔给我们带来面条、陈面包块和火柴。他们甚至给了我们一条毛巾。
7月14日，另一名受害者加入了我们。他是G. 缅什克（G. Menshik），苏联公民，北洋报社（Peiyang Press）雇员。当天上午8:30，他在去办公室的路上，科兹洛夫斯基要求他去警察局接受问话。鉴于此前有过类似经历，缅什克同意了。然而，他被直接带到了“Russkiy Dom”。在那里，他被询问关于苏联领事馆的情况、他与苏联领事馆的关系，以及他为何为一家德国公司北洋报社工作。他还遭到了严厉殴打。
两天后，即7月16日，当我们被带到前德国公园的中国警察分局总部时，他的状况极其糟糕。在这里，我们有两个房间和木地板，对此我们心存感激。
缅什克无法起身。他的肾脏部位遭到无情殴打，导致无法排尿。他的腹部和眼睛肿胀，似乎随时都会爆裂。他有一半时间处于昏迷状态。

On the afternoon of July 27, Japan-
ese gendarmes, bearing a banner, marched
us through the ex-German Concession to
the Lushan Maru. We embarked at 4
p.m., but the Japanese, reinforced by
Chinese uniformed policemen, stood on
the wharf with drawn firearms until 8
p.m., when the boat sailed from the Ger-
man Bund.
PRISONER LEAPS
TO FREEDOM
As the vessel was turning, Victor
Krivoroochko leaped overboard and swam
some 10 yards which separated the boat
from the British Bund. We saw him
reach it safely.
The captain of the Lushan Maru was
given papers to the effect that we were
Soviet spies, for which we were being de-
ported to Shanghai. Fortunately for us,
when we reached Shanghai on August 3.
the captain took pity on us and did not
show our papers.
Thanks to several friends here, who
have made medical treatment possible, I
am recovering from my nightmare ex-
perience. My lungs and kidneys and
other organs have been seriously afflicted
by the severe beatings, to an extent
which even I did not realize.
I cannot even presume why our own
Russian in North China are persecuting
their fellow-emigrants with such bestial-
ity, but the common belief there is that
Major Taki, the Japanese at the head of
the "Russian" organization, insists on the
capture of Soviet spies. Since it is their
bread and butter to produce results, they
do so with a complete disregard for truth
or facts, obtaining sworn statements with
brutal methods which, I had thought, had
passed and remained only in stories of
the dark, medieval ages.

7月27日下午，日本宪兵举着旗帜，押解我们穿过前德租界，前往庐山丸号（Lushan Maru）。我们在下午4点登船，但由身穿制服的中国警察增援的日本人在码头上持枪警戒，直到晚上8点船只从德国外滩启航。
囚犯跳向自由
当船只转弯时，维克多·克里沃鲁奇科跳入水中，游过了分隔船只与英国外滩的大约10码距离。我们看到他安全抵达。
庐山丸号的船长持有文件，称我们为苏联间谍，因此我们将被驱逐至上海。幸运的是，当我们于8月3日抵达上海时，船长对我们产生了怜悯，没有出示我们的文件。
多亏这里的几位朋友使医疗救治成为可能，我正从那场噩梦般的经历中恢复过来。我的肺部、肾脏和其他器官因遭受严重殴打而受到严重损害，其程度甚至超出了我之前的认知。
我甚至无法揣测为何我们在华北的俄国同胞会以如此兽行迫害他们的流亡同胞，但那里的普遍看法是，领导该“俄国”组织的日本人高木少佐（Major Taki）坚持要抓捕苏联间谍。由于制造成果是他们的生计所在，他们完全不顾真相或事实，通过残酷的手段获取宣誓供词，而我原以为这种手段早已过去，只存在于黑暗的中世纪故事中。
